tasks.instruction: The examiner will ask you some questions about you and your free time. Answer each question clearly and give some details.

choices.title: Interview about you and your weekends
choices.prompt: Imagine you are meeting the examiner for the first time. The examiner asks about your home, your daily life and a recent weekend.
bullets: Where you live and what you do
What you like doing on the weekend

turns.ask: Good morning. Where do you live, and who do you live with?

points.label: Says where they live or who they live with

turns.model: I live in a small apartment in the city center with my sister.

turns.ask: What do you do? Do you work or study?

points.label: Says what they do: work or study

turns.model: I work in a small bookstore near my apartment. I'm a sales clerk, and I like my job.

turns.ask: What do you usually do on the weekend?

points.label: Names something they usually do on the weekend

turns.model: On Saturdays I usually play soccer with my friends, and on Sundays I visit my grandmother.

turns.ask: Do you prefer to stay at home or go out with friends? Why?

points.label: Says what they prefer and gives a reason

turns.model: I prefer to go out with my friends because it's more fun than staying at home alone.

turns.ask: Now, tell me something about last weekend. What did you do, who was with you, and how was it?

points.label: Says what they did last weekend

turns.model: Last weekend was really nice. On Saturday I went to the beach with my family. We swam in the sea and ate fish for lunch. On Sunday I met my friends in a café and we watched a movie. I enjoyed it a lot because I was very relaxed.

tasks.instruction: Look at the five ways of getting around a city. The examiner will talk with you about them. Give your opinion and say why.

choices.title: Discussion: getting around the city
choices.prompt: Here are five ways of getting around a city. The examiner asks you five questions about them. Answer each one with your own ideas and experience.
bullets: A time you used one of them
choices.input:
Getting around a city

1. Walking
2. The bus
3. A bicycle
4. A taxi
5. The subway

turns.ask: Look at the five ways to travel in a city. Which one do you use most often, and why?

points.label: Names the way they use most

turns.model: I use the bus most often, because it goes directly from my house to my office and it is not expensive.

turns.ask: Which of these ways is the cheapest? Why do you think so?

points.label: Talks about the cost of the ways to travel

turns.model: I think walking is the cheapest, because you don't pay anything. A bike is cheap too, but a taxi costs a lot of money.

turns.ask: Which way is the fastest, and which one is the most comfortable?
turns.model: The subway is the fastest, because there is no traffic. For me the most comfortable is a taxi, because I can sit and relax.

turns.ask: Tell me about the last time you traveled across a city. Where did you go?

points.label: Tells about a past trip in a city

turns.model: Last week I went to the museum with my brother. We took the subway because the museum is far from my house, and it was quick.

turns.ask: What could your city do to make traveling easier? Give me one idea.

points.label: Gives an idea to improve travel in the city

turns.model: I think the city should build more bike lanes, so people can ride safely. It would also be good to have cheaper tickets for the bus.
